verdict.rationale: DBOS documents step checkpointing so recovery resumes from the last completed step without re-running succeeded work. Community reports describe @DBOS.Transaction giving exactly-once execution and a Kafka pipeline processed exactly once per message. However, no first-party evidence documents idempotency keys or deduplication of duplicate external triggers, and durability is bounded by the Postgres configuration. Missing for 10: documented idempotency-key or workflow-ID deduplication for duplicate triggers, first-party docs on exactly-once guarantees for non-transactional side effects such as payments or emails, and hands-on corroboration that double-charging or double-sending is prevented.

support.subject: As a backend developer, idempotency keys and exactly-once step semantics stop duplicate triggers from double-charging or double-sending

citations.quote: Because every task is checkpointed, your agent can recover from any failure mid-flight without re-running work that already succeeded.
DBOS uses this checkpointed state to recover each of your workflows from its last completed step.
its @DBOS.Transaction decorator runs steps inside a Postgres transaction for exactly-once execution
